throughput_recovery.headline: 4–8% throughput, 1–3pp recovery
throughput_recovery.figure: opportunities to raise mineral recovery by 1 to 3 percent and increase throughput by 4 to 8 percent, while reducing energy consumption
throughput_recovery.aside: a productivity boost of 5 to 10 percent, which equates roughly to opening a new mine without the capital cost
throughput_recovery.title: Behind the mining productivity upswing: Technology-enabled transformation
throughput_recovery.scope: Available uplift from technology-enabled transformation across mining operations, not attributed to any single technology.

throughput_100_assets.headline: Recovery up 1–3 percentage points
throughput_100_assets.figure: potential to achieve 8 to 10 percent in throughput improvement as well as an uptick of one to three percentage points in recovery
throughput_100_assets.aside: alongside 8 to 10 percent throughput improvement, observed across more than 100 assets across industries and commodities globally
throughput_100_assets.title: Advancing metals and mining in Southeast Asia with digital and analytics
throughput_100_assets.scope: Observed across a stated base of 100+ assets, which makes this the best evidenced of the throughput figures.

haulage_ahs.headline: 20% productivity improvement from autonomous haulage
haulage_ahs.figure: miners using autonomous haulage technology have reported a 20 percent improvement in productivity
haulage_ahs.title: Behind the mining productivity upswing: Technology-enabled transformation
haulage_ahs.scope: Reported by Western Australian operators running autonomous haulage fleets. It is a fleet-automation figure, not a decision-support one.

procurement.headline: Procurement productivity up to 50%
procurement.figure: improved their procurement productivity by up to 50%
procurement.title: Racing Toward a Digital Future in Metals and Mining
procurement.scope: Upper end of a range observed among digitally mature metals and mining companies; quoted as a ceiling, not a typical result.

quartile_gap.headline: Top-quartile sites run 6% higher truck availability than average
quartile_gap.figure: companies with scores in the top quartile of the OHI had truck availability that was 8 percent higher than companies in the bottom quartile, and 6 percent higher than average OHI performers
quartile_gap.aside: that 8 percent difference could translate into a production increase of around 5 percent, or a decrease in operations costs of about 2 percent
quartile_gap.title: The missing link in mining-company productivity: People
quartile_gap.scope: Cross-mine benchmark linking Organizational Health Index quartile to physical equipment performance. The gap is attributed to operational discipline and accountability, not to technology.

discipline_gap.headline: 16% higher effective equipment use, on discipline alone
discipline_gap.figure: top quartile results in 'Accountability' and 'Operational discipline' achieved 16 percent higher UEE than those in the bottom quartile
discipline_gap.title: The missing link in mining-company productivity: People
discipline_gap.scope: Utilisation of Equipment Effectiveness, quartile to quartile. Named here because consistency of practice, not new plant, is what moves it.

digital_maturity.headline: Mining is 30–40% less digitally mature than comparable industries
digital_maturity.figure: the metals and mining industry is roughly 30% to 40% less digitally mature than comparable industries
digital_maturity.aside: some improved their mining throughput by 10% to 20% and their procurement productivity by up to 50%
digital_maturity.title: Racing Toward a Digital Future in Metals and Mining
digital_maturity.scope: Based on BCG's Digital Acceleration Index survey of large metals and mining companies.

productivity_decline.headline: 28% less efficient at moving a tonne than a decade earlier
productivity_decline.figure: mining productivity as measured by MPI has declined 3.5 percent per year, meaning mining companies are 28 percent less efficient in digging and moving a ton of total material today than ten years ago
productivity_decline.title: Productivity in mining operations: Reversing the downward trend
productivity_decline.scope: Industry-wide index over the decade to 2015. Used to establish that the gap is an industry condition rather than a failing of one operator.

data_unused.headline: Miners use less than 1% of the data their equipment produces
data_unused.figure: miners use less than 1 percent of the information collected from their equipment
data_unused.aside: average overall equipment effectiveness of 27 percent for underground mining and 39 percent for open-pit, against 88 percent for upstream oil and gas
data_unused.title: How digital innovation can improve mining productivity
data_unused.scope: 2015 vintage; the OEE contrast is the durable part of the finding.

genai_reality.headline: Only ~5% of companies get a tenth of their EBIT from gen AI
genai_reality.figure: only about 5 percent of companies attribute at least 10 percent of their EBIT to gen AI
genai_reality.title: Mining for operational excellence
genai_reality.scope: Cross-industry. Printed deliberately: a case that only carries upside reads as a brochure, and this is the figure a sceptical chief executive already has in mind before the meeting starts.
